title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Georgetown rituals spanning senior portraits, Hilltop Halloween, school spirit, community celebrations and student performance.

cards.title: Take the Senior Lap Photo
cards.subtitle: A pre-graduation portrait with Georgetown’s founder
cards.notes: Near graduation, photograph the tradition from ground level and treat the historic statue carefully; avoid climbing if conditions are unsafe.
cards.short_summary: Seniors mark their final spring by posing in the seated founder’s lap before leaving the Hilltop.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown identifies sitting in John Carroll’s lap before graduation, with a photograph, as a well-known student tradition.
cards.access_notes: The statue stands in Healy Circle on Georgetown’s private Hilltop Campus; follow posted campus-access rules.

cards.title: Close the Semester on Georgetown Day
cards.subtitle: The Hilltop’s annual university-wide spring celebration
cards.notes: Check the official program, then choose a daytime lawn activity or student performance that fits your schedule and accessibility needs.
cards.short_summary: Students, faculty and staff gather near semester’s end for a full day of Hilltop activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown’s Center for Student Engagement says Georgetown Day began in 2000 and is an annual university-wide celebration held at the end of each spring semester.
cards.access_notes: Open to Georgetown students, faculty and staff; consult the current annual program for locations and entry conditions.

cards.title: Pause Finals for Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: A study-days breakfast served after dark at Leo’s
cards.notes: Bring your Georgetown identification, confirm the semester’s announced time and use the meal as a deliberate break from studying.
cards.short_summary: Once each semester, Hoyas step away from study days for complimentary late-night breakfast together.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown lists Midnight Breakfast as a signature event held each semester during study days at Leo’s, with free late-night breakfast for students.
cards.access_notes: Held during study days at Leo’s; verify the current semester’s date, eligibility and late-night entry instructions.

cards.title: See Rangila Fill Gaston Hall
cards.subtitle: Georgetown’s annual student-run South Asian dance showcase
cards.notes: Reserve through the announced ticket channel, arrive before curtain and look for the program’s mix of regional and fusion choreography.
cards.short_summary: Hundreds of students rehearse and perform an annual philanthropic celebration of South Asian dance and music.
cards.evidence_claim: A 2024 Georgetown account describes Rangila as an annual philanthropic South Asian dance showcase and identifies that edition as the event’s 30th.
cards.source_title: A Backstage Look at Rangila 30, Georgetown’s South Asian Dance Show
cards.access_notes: Performance access and ticketing vary by year; consult the current Rangila announcement before attending.

cards.title: Start Homecoming with Traditions Day
cards.subtitle: A Copley and Healy lawns kickoff centered on Hoya customs
cards.notes: Consult the Homecoming program, then begin on Copley or Healy Lawn and use the event to identify traditions represented that year.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming Weekend opens with a lawn gathering devoted explicitly to Georgetown traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown’s Center for Student Engagement states that Traditions Day kicks off Homecoming Weekend on Copley and Healy lawns and celebrates university traditions.
cards.access_notes: Part of Homecoming Weekend; verify the current program, weather plan and participant eligibility.

cards.title: Enter Haunted Healy
cards.subtitle: The Programming Board’s Halloween takeover of Healy Hall
cards.notes: Use only the staffed event entrance, follow volunteer directions and skip the attraction if flashing lights or staged scares are unsuitable.
cards.short_summary: For decades, students have transformed part of Healy Hall into a supervised seasonal haunted house.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown reported in 2023 that the Georgetown Programming Board had hosted Haunted Healy for 40 years, converting Healy Hall’s second floor into a haunted house.
cards.source_title: The Best Halloween Traditions at Georgetown
cards.access_notes: Attend only when officially scheduled and supervised; Healy Hall access outside the programmed route is restricted.

cards.entity_name: The Exorcist Screening on Copley Lawn
cards.title: Watch The Exorcist Where Its Story Lives
cards.subtitle: Georgetown’s annual outdoor Halloween-eve film screening
cards.notes: Check the Programming Board announcement, bring weather-appropriate layers and choose seating that permits an easy exit from the horror film.
cards.short_summary: The campus connection to The Exorcist becomes an annual late-night movie gathering on Copley Lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown documented that the Programming Board hosts a late-night screening of The Exorcist on Copley Lawn every year on the night before Halloween.
cards.source_title: The Best Halloween Traditions at Georgetown
cards.access_notes: The documented screening is late at night; verify the current start time, weather status and campus eligibility before attending.

cards.title: Howl at Midnight on Halloween
cards.subtitle: A post-screening chorus beside Georgetown’s Jesuit Cemetery
cards.notes: Join only the organized group after the screening, remain on open paths and respect the Jesuit Cemetery as an active memorial space.
cards.short_summary: As Halloween begins, students gather after the film and answer midnight with a communal howl.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown describes the Healy Howl as a tradition in which students go to the Jesuit graveyard after The Exorcist screening and howl when midnight begins Halloween.
cards.source_title: The Best Halloween Traditions at Georgetown
cards.access_notes: This is a midnight tradition; stay with the organized group, use established paths and obey current cemetery-access rules.

cards.title: Take Halloween to Embassy Row
cards.subtitle: A Georgetown student tradition shaped by studying in Washington
cards.notes: Confirm each embassy’s public invitation before traveling, carry identification and visit only posted public entrances during stated hours.
cards.short_summary: Hoyas extend Halloween beyond the Hilltop by visiting participating diplomatic missions for treats and cultural exchange.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown’s student-life blog says trick-or-treating at embassies has been a Georgetown student tradition for years and documents visits to three embassies.
cards.source_title: The Best Halloween Traditions at Georgetown
cards.access_notes: Participation is embassy-specific and not guaranteed; verify current public access, security requirements and hours directly.

cards.title: Answer the Crowd with Hoya Saxa
cards.subtitle: Georgetown’s century-old Greek-and-Latin cheer
cards.notes: Listen for the pep band’s cue at an official game, follow the student section’s cadence and treat the debated origin as unresolved history.
cards.short_summary: A hybrid-language yell first printed in the 1890s still supplies Georgetown’s defining game-day response.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown reported in 2025 that “Hoya Saxa” means “what rocks” and has served as the university’s cheer for more than 100 years.
cards.source_title: What Being a Hoya Means to the 2025-2026 Georgetown Storytellers
cards.access_notes: Most readily heard at official athletics events; event admission and venue rules vary by game.
